---
title: Gradient Checkpointing
description: Gradient checkpointing in Axolotl is configured and documented as activation checkpointing.
---

::: {.callout-note}
## This page has moved

Gradient checkpointing is now documented under
[Activation Checkpointing & Offloading](activation_checkpointing.qmd).
:::

Gradient checkpointing and activation checkpointing are two names for the same technique. During
the forward pass each decoder layer keeps only its input and drops its intermediate activations;
during the backward pass it runs its forward again to rebuild them. Activation memory drops to
about one hidden-state tensor per layer, at the cost of roughly one extra forward pass per step.

PyTorch, DeepSpeed, accelerate and transformers (from 5.23) call it activation checkpointing, and
Axolotl's config follows them: `activation_checkpointing: true` replaces
`gradient_checkpointing: true`, which still works but is deprecated, and the same block configures
selective checkpointing and activation offloading.

```yaml
activation_checkpointing: true
```
